title: 2015 AMC 10B Problem 9
statement: The shaded region below is called a shark’s fin falcata, a figure studied by Leonardo da Vinci. It is bounded by the portion of the circle of radius \(3\) and center \((0,0)\) that lies in the first quadrant, the portion of the circle with radius \(\tfrac{3}{2}\) and center \((0,\tfrac{3}{2})\) that lies in the first quadrant, and the line segment from \((0,0)\) to \((3,0).\) What is the area of the shark’s fin falcata?

solutions.text:
The larger boundary is a quarter circle of radius \(3\), so its area is \(\frac14\pi\cdot3^2=\frac{9\pi}{4}\).

The inner boundary is the right half of a circle of radius \(\frac32\), so its area is \(\frac12\pi\left(\frac32\right)^2=\frac{9\pi}{8}\).

The shaded area is the difference, \(\frac{9\pi}{4}-\frac{9\pi}{8}=\frac{9\pi}{8}\).

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Subtract the smaller semicircle from the larger quarter circle
